channel.title: Wisconsin Newspaper Association - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Wisconsin Newspaper Association (wnanews.com)

item.title: Former Crawford County Independent & Kickapoo Scout journalist earns Devroy Fellowship
item.description: Ambrosia Wojahn, who worked at The Crawford County Independent & Kickapoo Scout while attending Laurel High School in Viroqua, has been chosen as the winner of the Ann Devroy Fellowship.

item.title: Journal Sentinel to host March 7 panel discussion about guns
item.description: The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel will co-sponsor an open panel discussion about guns at 10 a.m. on March 7 at Most Worshipful Prince Hall Grand Lodge State of Wisconsin at Prince Hall Masonic Temple, which is located at 1218 W. North Ave. on Milwaukee’s north side.

item.title: WisEye bill clears Assembly but faces competing bill in Senate
item.description: Bipartisan legislation to give WisconsinEye, the state’s version of C-SPAN, taxpayer funds to publicly broadcast state government functions unanimously cleared the state Assembly on Tuesday, Feb. 10.

item.title: Snow much fun: Winter adventures around Wisconsin
item.description: Your next winter adventure is just a drive away: This snowy season, buckle up and discover Wisconsin’s counties.

item.title: Former Union Grove Sun Times journalist dies
item.description: A March 15, 2026 Celebration of Life is planned for former Union Grove Sun Times journalist and editor Jacqueline M. Seitz, who died Feb. 9 at age 91.

item.title: Presque Isle turns over records after DA’s ultimatum
item.description: After the Vilas County district attorney took the rare step of issuing an ultimatum, the town of Presque Isle met a Jan. 30 deadline for turning over requested records to The Lakeland Times.

item.title: Piwowarczyk transparency, accountability bills pass Assembly
item.description: State Rep. Jim Piwowarczyk, R-Town of Erin, had four bills passed by the State Assembly, on Thursday, which aim to make government more accountable and transparent. The four bills included Assembly Bill (AB) 669, AB 757, AB 907 and AB 908.

item.title: Evers’ final State of State address spells out goals for the rest of his term
item.description: Democratic Gov. Tony Evers, in his final State of the State address, emphasized past accomplishments, poked and prodded GOP lawmakers and laid out goals for the months remaining in his last year in office.

item.title: New limits on student cellphones in Wisconsin schools
item.description: Starting July 1, 2026, every Wisconsin public school district must limit student use of personal cellphones and other wireless devices during instructional time. Let's review what parents should know.

item.title: Sunshine Week 2026 toolkit available online
item.description: Sunshine Week, set for March 15-21, 2026, is a nonpartisan collaboration among groups in the journalism, civic, education, government and private sectors that shines a light on the importance of public records and open government.
